resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. strategy_tie_in §4 (strategy-fidelity; Big Idea and mood facets) line 27: scope: The finding is filed under the wrong rule. I read check_strategy_tie_in.md §4 at its current wording. It is "Strategy-fidelity check": pull per-module sequencing claims from the content-strategy doc ("first X lands at module N", "no Y before module M") and verify the draft does not front-run a downstream teaching moment. The judge's harm is different. It says two sentences are missing and the maintainer note is stale. That is not front-running a later module. Nothing at L27-L29 pre-teaches or leaks anything from a later module, so §4 is not violated. The judge's "Big Idea and mood facets" gloss is not §4's text. Mood is §1 and the Big Idea belongs to other items. §1's mood-floor is also only a per-beat 8+/10 score, and the judge did not score it.

The factual claims are true, but they do not make a §4 BLOCK:
- The body lacks the McKinsey sentence and the "Before today, you had a vocabulary... felt experience" sentence.
- Maintainer L38 still says the beat ends on the felt-experience sentence and that the McKinsey beat stays verbatim.
- blend.md L75-79 says to cut only the second half of "Mental models only come from doing" and to keep the McKinsey line.

The cuts are not unauthorised drift. Commit 816efb6c (2026-11-01, "compaction pass") made them. The preceding commits 25c825e3 and 6ddd58ec still had both sentences. That pass follows a dated maintainer steer recorded in curriculum/language/rewrite-rules.md ("compacted, compacted... training slides need to be able to be glanced"). The language compaction report shows the same McKinsey slide flagged as over its sentence budget (14 sentences, 1 over), with the McKinsey line in the register flags. This is a maintainer-directed density pass on a slide-rendered lecture, not a strategy-fidelity regression. The locked-sentences gate passes ("4 locked sentences intact") and none of the locks cover these sentences. Nothing in the file or the rule says the closer's last claim must carry a felt-experience payload, and the "You act on the future to know what's real" claim and its Big Idea beat are intact. / harm: The facts the judge cites are accurate. The conclusion does not hold, because the cut was deliberate and the rule is the wrong one.

Facts I checked:
- The body at L27-29 has neither the McKinsey sentence nor the felt-experience sentence.
- Maintainer L38 still says the mental-models beat "ends on the felt-experience sentence" and that "the McKinsey beat stays verbatim".
- blend.md § Titles M1 says "Cut the second half of *Mental models only come from doing*... Keep the McKinsey line."
- Both sentences were removed in commit 816efb6c (2026-11-01), "Agents 101 M1: compaction pass to main". `git log -p` shows the diff cutting "Reading a McKinsey report... Running the experiment gives you experience of it" and "Before today, you had a vocabulary. Now you have a little piece of felt experience."
- That commit message says the pass was measured at n=24 (language 63 to 89, loop overall 61 to 80, Big Idea 67 vs 75 baseline, which it calls noise). It also says a fuller rewrite was kept in scratch because it scored lower on the Big Idea.

Why it fails the harm lens:
(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. The student has just done the exercise, so the felt experience is delivered by the exercise. The slide's claim, "Mental models only come from doing", is a one-line closer that restates what they just did. The cut McKinsey line was a rhetorical contrast, not load-bearing teaching.
(b) The finding is a restatement of a mismatch between files. blend.md dates from 2026-09. The measured compaction pass of 2026-11-01 postdates it and supersedes it. There is no student-facing consequence.
(c) The proposed fix would reverse a measured, deliberate compaction. It would also re-add language that the sentence-level language loop pruned.
(d) The "act on the future / run the experiment" meaning is still carried by L27, and the doing is carried by L29 and the exercise.

The cited rule does not fit. check_strategy_tie_in §4 is the strategy-fidelity check against front-running downstream modules, meaning per-module sequencing claims. The body front-runs nothing. L27 contains no forward promise, and the closer explicitly carries none.

What remains is housekeeping, not a blocker. Maintainer L38 is stale: it describes content the 2026-11-01 compaction removed. It should say the McKinsey sentence and the felt-experience sentence were cut in 816efb6c. It should also record the header renames, namely `The agent generated, you decided` in place of the blend's `You were the only check in the room`, and `look-back` in place of `retro`; L40 already covers `look-back`. Maintainer blocks apply directly with no approval card, and the student body needs no change.
